d: Ektis is a boutique financial services consulting firm operating at the heart of the GCC's financial ecosystem. We partner with banks, fintechs, development finance institutions, and public-sector clients to solve their most critical challenges - spanning strategy, commercial growth, risk, payments, and transformation.

Provide continuous, independent finance monitoring of the economics and revenue lifecycle of Ektis client engagements. Build a reliable view of what was priced and contracted, what is being delivered, what may be recognized and billed, what has been invested, and where margin, scope,cashor control risks areemerging. The role informs and challengesdecision-makers; engagement partners and teamsretainclient, commercial and delivery accountability, and Financeretainsaccounting-policyand ledger responsibilities.
q: Experience in professional-services finance, project economics, commercial finance, revenue assurance or engagement management in a consulting, technology, legal, engineering or similar services firm.
Strong grasp of time-based and fixed/bill-based service economics, realization, utilization, WIP, margin, subcontractor costs, contract changes and billing dependencies.

Advanced spreadsheet/reporting skills and CRM, project/time or ERP data experience are useful; able to challenge with evidence and distinguish fact from estimate. Legal interpretation remains with counsel.
Arabic reading, writing and speaking skills strongly preferred
r: Establish a controlled engagement record from opportunity and approved estimate through contract/SOW, engagement setup, delivery, change control, billing, collection and closure. Salesforce and other applicable systems are expected to support this control environment; the operating model must work through a controlled interim register where systems are not yet available.

Reconcile the engagement record to signed contract terms, approved proposals, amendments, purchase orders or client portal records, approved budgets and Finance records. Identify missing or contradictory data; label fields as stated, calculated, not stated or in conflict, and route clarification to the accountable owner instead of filling gaps by assumption.

Track contracted value and fee basis separately from out-of-pocket expenses, VAT/tax, reimbursables and other pass-through items. Capture currency, entity, contract period, billing rights, milestones, acceptance conditions and client-specific requirements.
Maintain a portfolio view of contract value, approved changes, extensions, remaining fees, committed delivery cost, revenue forecast, invoice status and client investment.

Review engagement price estimates and business cases for completeness, assumptions, staffing mix, grade/rate logic, utilization, subcontractor inputs, duration, delivery risk, client value and expected margin before the authorized approval.

Maintain analysis of discounts, fixed-fee and capped-fee exposure, contingency, success or contingent-fee features, write-off assumptions and any commercial concessions. Escalate departures from policy or delegated authority.

Track approved price changes, scope variations, contract extensions, change requests and unbilled work against signed evidence and authority. Flag delivery activity that appears outside scope or without a documented commercial route.
Provide pricing and margin insight to partners and CFO, but do not set the client price, negotiate/approve commercial terms or bypass engagement-partner accountability.
Revenue recognition, WIP and billing monitoring

Monitor time-based and bill-based revenue drivers, approved milestones, client acceptance, time capture, WIP, unbilled revenue, billed amounts, write-ups, write-downs, provisions and write-offs against Ektis policy and documented engagement facts.

Prepare recurring engagement-level exceptions and explain movements between contract value, delivered work, recognized revenue, WIP, invoice and cash status. Distinguish operational monitoring from accounting entries and technical accounting judgments.
Coordinate with Finance on revenue recognition policy, month-end estimates, provisions and ledger treatment; ensure any estimate has a documented basis, reviewer and approved accounting treatment.

Monitor invoice readiness, milestone acceptance evidence, client purchase order coverage, portal or billing instructions, overdue queries and blocked invoices. Escalate risk before the monthly close or contractual billing window is missed.
Delivery economics, margin and client investment

Compare approved engagement economics with actual and forecast effort, realization, delivery mix, utilization, subcontractor and contingent workforce cost, travel/out-of-pocket items, write-downs and expected margin.

Identify margin erosion, scope creep, over-servicing, low realization, under-recovery, delayed acceptance, poor time capture, pricing leakage and concentration or collection exposure. Quantify exposure using a disclosed calculation and source data.

Monitor net investment in clients through unbilled work, WIP, receivables, disputed invoices, credit notes, provisions and time to cash; coordinate with partners and Treasury on actions while respecting ownership of collection relationships.
Provide practical review packs for engagement partners and CFO that distinguish trend, exception, decision needed, action owner and due date. Follow actions through resolution.

Maintain minimum engagement data, ownership, workflow and evidence requirements with Finance, partners, delivery teams, Sales/CRM and technology owners. Do not select or configure systems without the appropriate programme and owner approvals.
Prepare a portfolio dashboard and targeted high-risk engagement reviews; establish escalation triggers with the CFO and partners once baseline data and risk appetite are agreed.
Maintain controlled definitions for contracted value, fees, revenue basis, WIP, write-up/down, margin, utilization, net client investment and material exception; document data limitations.

Escalate suspected misstatement, unsupported billing, unapproved discount/variation, repeated scope breach or other potentially improper practice promptly to the CFO and relevant partner, preserving evidence and confidentiality.

Saudi Arabia is Foodics' biggest market and needs a leader who can bring both strategic rigor and creative excellence: someone who plans and budgets like an operator, thinks and owns revenue like a growth leader, and still has the creative instincts to produce campaigns that resonate with the market.
Full marketing strategy and execution for the Saudi Arabia market, with direct accountability to the VP of Marketing.
Planning and budgeting for the Saudi marketing function, including forecasting, resource allocation, and performance tracking against revenue and growth goals.
Leadership of a team of three (Social, PR & Communications, and Events), plus management of an external creative/marketing agency.
Creative direction and content production, working closely with the agency to deliver high-quality, on-brand campaigns.
Close cross-functional collaboration with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, and Communications to ensure a unified go-to-market approach.
Coordination with Sales and Customer Success in Saudi Arabia to align marketing activity with pipeline, revenue, and merchant retention goals.
Deep, active relationships with merchants in the Saudi F&B community, using market presence to inform strategy and unlock opportunities.
Positioning Foodics around its mission and value — as a strategic partner to F&B businesses — rather than competing purely as a point-of-sale commodity.
A clear, well-structured marketing plan for the Saudi market, built and owned end-to-end.
Creative output that is relevant and tied to business outcomes — not creative for its own sake.
Demonstrated ownership of revenue impact, with a growth-hacking mindset applied to the Saudi market.
Foodics established as a clear leader in the Saudi F&B community.

d: The Parts Logistics Manager is responsible for leading the strategic planning, governance, and optimization of spare parts logistics, warehousing, and distribution across all branches and depots. This role ensures accurate forecasting, timely replenishment, and full lifecycle control of parts to support operational continuity and service excellence. By overseeing ERP systems, supplier performance, and logistics analytics, the manager drives cost efficiency, minimizes downtime, and ensures compliance with internal and regulatory standards. Acting as the central liaison between inventory planning, procurement, warehouse, aftersales, and finance teams, the Parts Logistics Manager builds scalable frameworks that future-proof logistics operations and align with business growth and industry evolution.
q: Certification in Logistics, Inventory Management, or ERP systems is a plus.
Minimum 5 years of experience in parts logistics and inventory management
Prior experience working with a Principal supplier is highly desirable
Experience managing 3PL contracts and international freight is essential
Experience with Saudi customs and regulatory compliance (ZATCA, SASO, SABER) is required
Strategic mindset with strong governance orientation.
Advanced skills in spare parts logistics, warehousing, and stock optimization.
Strong cross-functional collaboration, communication, and stakeholder management.
Proven ability to implement preventive measures, enforce compliance, and drive efficiency.
Integrity, attention to detail, and commitment to continuous improvement.
r: Establish and maintain a unified logistics control framework across all branches and depots, ensuring real-time visibility of stock levels, part movements, and supply status.
Develop and enforce Group-wide logistics policies covering inbound, outbound, and reverse logistics, warehousing, replenishment, VOR handling, and compliance.
Oversee integration and continuous enhancement of ERP and logistics systems to enable end-to-end digital tracking, forecasting, and reporting.
Direct end-to-end spare parts logistics across UMG network in Saudi Arabia, managing an inventory portfolio across 50,000+ SKUs.
Oversee inbound, outbound, and reverse logistics operations, ensuring seamless movement of parts from suppliers to warehouses, warehouses to branches, between branches, and branches to warehouse.
Hold end-to-end accountability for 4PL multi-client CPD warehouse in Jeddah, operated via 3rd party, ensuring inventory integrity and distribution to 40+ dealer and branch locations nationwide.
Direct international freight strategy across ocean, air, and land, optimizing cost, transit time, and service levels across a global supplier base.
Ensure smooth and timely distribution to all branches, minimizing lead times and ensuring service continuity.
Manage vendor/service provider contracts, driving SLA compliance, commercial negotiation, and cost accountability.
Drive warehousing and logistics operations toward cost optimization, risk mitigation, and a future-ready supply chain supporting the group's growth.
Ensure full regulatory compliance with Saudi customs and product standards, including ZATCA, SASO, and SABER (PCOC & SCOC).
Ensure all necessary permits are available and maintained for logistics and warehousing operations.
Manage QHSE compliance across all logistics and warehousing activities.
Oversee Dangerous Goods (DG) items handling compliance, ensuring safe storage, transportation, and documentation.
Monitor supplier performance, lead times, and exception handling to ensure timely and cost-effective parts availability.
Identify and mitigate risks related to pricing and supply chain disruptions.
Extract and analyze logistics and inventory data from ERP and supplier systems to maintain a predictive, actionable overview of stock health.
Deliver strategic insights to senior management through dashboards and reports covering SOH, fill rate, lead time, backorders, and inventory value.
Support monthly and quarterly reviews with performance metrics and improvement recommendations.
Act as the central liaison for logistics-related matters, ensuring alignment between aftersales parts, service, warehouse, finance, and IT teams.
Provide guidance and policy enforcement to branch-level logistics teams, ensuring consistency and operational excellence.
Facilitate cross-functional planning meetings to align logistics strategy with business goals and service targets.
Build strong relationships with principal suppliers and work closely with them.
Continuously evolve the logistics management model to incorporate automation, predictive analytics, and digital transformation.
Evaluate and implement logistics planning tools and ERP enhancements tailored to automotive spare parts operations.
Build scalable frameworks that future-proof logistics control against business growth, regulatory changes, and market volatility.
